title: hyperv: add timeout to vsock ready wait
body:
## Problem

When you run `podman machine init` or `podman machine start` on Windows (HyperV), Podman has to wait for the guest VM to say "I'm ready" through a socket connection called hvsock.

The function `HVSockRegistryEntry.ListenSetupWait()` in `pkg/machine/hyperv/vsock/vsock.go` starts a background goroutine (`sockets.ListenAndWaitOnSocket`) that waits for the guest to connect and say it's ready, then just does `return <-errChan`. This blocks with no timeout at all. So if the guest VM is still running but never actually reaches the point where it signals ready (say some service inside the guest hangs), there is simply no way for this wait to end on its own. Nothing above it in the code has a timeout either, so the whole thing can hang forever.

I checked this myself by testing `sockets.ListenAndWaitOnSocket` directly against a real `net.Listener` that never gets connected to, no Hyper-V or actual guest VM involved, and confirmed it never returns.

## Proposed fix

Take the actual waiting part out into its own small function, `waitForReady(errChan, timeout)`, and add a timeout using `time.After`. If the wait goes on longer than `readyTimeout` (5 minutes), it stops waiting and returns a clear error instead of hanging forever.

5 minutes gives plenty of extra time for a normal, healthy boot to finish. I pulled 10 real successful `podman machine init --now` runs from Podman's own Hyper-V CI (run 31508856317), and they cluster tightly between 15.8s and 19.4s, so 5 minutes is generous headroom over that without hanging with no end.

## Testing done so far

I tested `waitForReady` by itself, covering three cases: it works normally, it passes through an error correctly, and it times out correctly. None of these tests need real Hyper-V.

I also added a fourth test that recreates the actual bug using a real `net.Listener` that never connects, and confirms the new timeout makes it return instead of hanging like before.

All of this runs natively on Windows, and both `go vet` and `go test` pass without any issues.

I have not been able to test this against a real Hyper-V guest VM end to end since I don't have that setup. This fix is only for the waiting logic itself, which doesn't depend on any specific platform, but the full `podman machine init` flow on an actual Hyper-V host should still be checked by CI or by a reviewer who has a Windows machine set up for it.

I'd like to open a PR with this fix, wanted to check the direction here first since I can't fully verify the real-VM path myself.
